4.2 Lane for high occupancy vehicles (VAO)
However, the Directorate General of Traffic (DGT) may also allow the use of the VAO lanes by the following vehicles, even when they are only occupied by their driver:
Taxis with an illuminated exterior sign and a current taxi licence.
Standard family cars classified as zero-emissions vehicles, ECO, C or B. This will be indicated on the variable message signs at the entrances to the VAO lanes.
Standard family cars classified as car-sharing (shared use vehicle).
The aforementioned standard family cars must be identified in all cases by the corresponding sticker.
(Página 164 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
5 Lanes reserved for certain manoeuvres
 
5.3 Exit or deceleration lanes
It is a special lane that allows drivers to exit a roadway and adjust their speed to the road they are joining and without obstructing the traffic flow on the road they are exiting. Normally this is located to the right of the roadway but in certain instances it may also be found on the left.
In order to leave a motorway or a dual carriageway drivers must:
Pay particular attention to the road signing and locate in advance their exit road.
Exit into the deceleration lane as soon as possible (where one is provided).
Reduce their speed within this lane, and without causing a hazard to other road users.
(Página 164 del manual 'Learning to drive')

7 Special circumstances regarding the circulation of traffic and the utilisation of lanes
 
7.2 Reversible lanes
Road users using these lanes must use (both day and night) at least the lowbeam headlights.
As a general rule, these lanes are not limited as to who can use them and the applicable speed limits are those of the roads on which they are located.
(Página 165 del manual 'Learning to drive')
